item.title: Scaling Agentic SDLC: Designing an Adaptive Auto Mode for Autonomous Coding
item.description:
Scaling Agentic SDLC: Designing an Adaptive Auto Mode for Autonomous Coding

In Part 1, I explained why moving from AI-first prompt engineering (VS Code + GitHub Copilot / OpenCode) to autonomous agentic coding (VS Code + Claude Code) breaks traditional software delivery, and why I built a strict Dual-PR Spec-First workflow for autonomous agents. By separating intent agreement from implementation execution, the architectural results were solid: zero contract drift, no test gaming, and strict boundary containment.

item.title: The Self-Declaration Principle: Why Handoffs Only Works When Agents Know Their Own Edges
item.description:
The Self-Declaration Principle: Why Handoffs Only Works When Agents Know Their Own Edges

After reading the LangChain taxonomy post and writing my own breakdown of the call-by-call numbers, I still had a nagging feeling I didn’t fully understand Handoffs. Not the mechanics — the handoff tool is simple enough. What I didn’t understand was why Handoffs produces the call-count advantages it claims, and under what conditions it actually behaves like the pattern the diagrams promise.
